messages:
maya: Quick q — security team asked about the retention plan for SIEM exports to our analytics partner. They want 7y archive for compliance but partner only accepts 2y. What are options?

jordan: short: split tiers. Keep 7y in cold encrypted archive (S3 Glacier-like) under our KMS, export only 2y to partner.

maya: Right, but compliance needs us to make 7y searchable for forensics. Partner doesn't need full access.

eli: We can keep raw logs in internal bucket `s3://redwood-sec-raw` with KMS CMK `alias/sec-logs`. Exports to partner go to `s3://partner-ingest` via export-proxy role that can only read objects tagged `exportable:true`.

ana: Tagging + lifecycle policy sounds good. Need process for scrubbing PII before export. Any recommendations for in-pipeline redaction?

jordan: Put a transform Lambda (or dataflow) step that applies field-level redaction using our PII ruleset. Use deterministic hashing for user IDs, remove SSNs, mask emails to `***@domain.com` if policy requires.

sec-bot: NOTE: export pipeline must add `x-audit-export: true` header and create an Audit Log entry for every exported file. (automated)

maya: About KMS: can we use a separate export key so partner can't request decrypt with our CMK? Or rotate per-export?

eli: Recommend envelope encryption: objects encrypted with an export-specific data key encrypted by an export-KMS key. We can rotate that key and revoke Grants when a contract ends. Also keep the raw bucket under a different CMK never shared.

ana: RBAC question: who gets access to the 7y archive for investigations? We want minimal blast radius but still let sec oncall pull artifacts.

jordan: Define an `sec-analyst` role with read-only S3 GetObject and `kms:Decrypt` on the raw CMK but require approval workflow (PR or JIT). Use Privileged Access Proxy for ephemeral credentials.

ops-oncall: Oncall needs fast access during incidents. Suggest a JIT path: file request -> approval -> temporary role for 1 hour with session tagging, and automated audit event creation.

maya: Sounds good. Also need retention enforcement: automatic deletion after 7y unless a legal hold exists.

eli: Add a `legal-hold` Dynamo record keyed by object prefix. Deletion pipeline checks hold before purge.

ana: For incident triage we sometimes need higher fidelity logs (full headers). Should those be kept in a separate high-fidelity store with tighter access?

jordan: Yes — separate high-fidelity store for sensitive headers + syscalls, access requires attestation. Very limited group, stricter KMS and access logs.

maya: Any objections to letting analytic partner keep aggregated metrics off exported data for >2y? They only need aggregates.

eli: Aggregates are fine, ensure they're one-way (cannot rehydrate PII). Prefer pre-aggregation on our side and export only summaries.

ana: Action items: 1) document tiered retention + life-cycle rules 2) implement export tagging + transform step 3) set up export-KMS + grant revocation flow 4) JIT access playbook 5) legal-hold check before deletion

jordan: I'll open a PR with the lifecycle JSON and a draft Lambda transform. ETA EOD tomorrow.

maya: Thanks — @ana please draft the JIT playbook and I'll sync with Legal about the hold process. :thumbsup:

ops-oncall: adding runbook link: https://confluence.redwood/infrasec/siem-export-runbook

sec-bot: Export audit event created: export_job_id=exp-20240307-42 user=maya

maya: Closing loop: we'll aim for implementation in next sprint and run tabletop DR that includes data restore from the 7y archive.
